sentence: This project studies how noncoding RNAs shape changes in epigenetic states as embryonic stem cells become neurons.
This project tests a preclinical treatment strategy that targets the ability of pancreas cancer to metastasize and the tumor microenvironment.
This project uses natural language processing to study how patterns in clinical documentation relate to outcomes for pregnant women and newborns.
This project builds an open standard and conversion tools so Optical Coherence Tomography imaging data can be shared across institutions.
This project links imaging technologies to research in cardiovascular medicine, from the individual molecule to the entire body.
This project studies how the host's immunostimulatory RNA helps the immune system defend against herpesvirus infection.
This project provides virology technologies, including microscopy and sequencing services, to help others collect data.
This project develops nonviral genome editing treatments for inherited retinal disorders that affect the retinal pigment epithelium.
This project uses advanced technology to analyze how survivors' traumatic memories, especially from adolescents, relate to their current mental health.
This project studies the mechanism of intracellular signal transduction, which is critical to processes such as cell growth and motility.
This project tries to find out how mutations in a gene that makes a protein maintaining ion gradients in neurons cause neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project tests small molecules that guide fusion proteins to the protein degradation machinery of the cell for destruction.
This project tests whether lysosomal targeting chimeras can degrade immune checkpoint proteins to improve radioimmunotherapy of head and neck cancer.
This project uses existing single-cell and whole genome sequencing datasets to map altered mRNA processing in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
This project develops a peptide-based hydrogel that delivers chemotherapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors locally to treat carcinomas.
This project studies common skin diseases such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and skin cancer, from basic to translational research.
This project develops genetically encoded sensors that monitor sex hormones in real time.
This project develops a system that makes large quantities of recombinant adenovirus-associated virus vectors in mammalian cells using a baculovirus-based expression system.
This project uses computer vision to build a navigation system for endoscopic sinus surgery that tracks instruments and updates computed tomography images.
This project builds computer software and datasets to study how DNA differences between people change how CRISPR works.
